text: A web-based platform for venue discovery, OTP authentication, booking workflow management, role-based dashboards, and future-ready integration support.
Introduction, existing system, scope, environment, technology, screens, and diagrams are organized in chapter order for major project delivery.
EMS2 digitizes the venue selection and booking process through a centralized web platform.
Customers can browse venues, compare price and capacity, authenticate with OTP, and move into a structured booking workflow from a single website.
The same platform helps owners manage venues and bookings while administrators supervise users, status, and overall platform activity.
The project is designed as more than a listing site: it is an integrated event venue management workflow.
Traditional venue booking often depends on phone calls, direct visits, notebooks, and disconnected records.
Customers must contact multiple venue providers separately to compare pricing, category, and date availability.
Owners may rely on notebooks or spreadsheets, which makes real-time status visibility weak and hard to coordinate.
Since information is fragmented, duplicate promises and booking conflicts can happen when multiple requests arrive together.
No single platform for comparison and progress tracking
Poor transparency in booking status and review visibility
A web-based event management platform is needed to replace the fragmented and error-prone manual workflow.
Users can access booking actions through a controlled login and verification flow.
Availability checks and temporary holds reduce overlapping booking requests.
Users, venues, bookings, reviews, and events are stored consistently.
Customers need faster venue discovery and better visibility into price, category, and status.
Owners need organized tools for listing management, slot updates, and booking review.
Administrators need role-based monitoring, user control, and system-wide operational oversight.
The project should remain extensible for AI recommendations and stronger payment automation.
The project scope covers functional platform behavior, technical architecture, and academic software engineering deliverables.
Browse venues, show details, register and log in with OTP, initiate bookings, track status, submit reviews, and manage dashboards.
Use PHP, MySQL, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in a modular controller-service-repository structure with external integration support.
Demonstrate requirement analysis, UML and flow diagrams, database design, implementation, testing, documentation, and user manuals.
Current limitations keep the focus on venue booking rather than full end-to-end event execution management.
The project runs in a standard web application setup and does not require specialized hardware.
Intel Core i3, i5, or higher
8 GB is recommended for smoother use
Free disk space for code, DB, and services
Needed for payment, mail, or SMS integrations
Standard monitor or laptop screen is sufficient for development and demonstration.
Keyboard and mouse support routine use, testing, and operator tasks.
The environment is practical for both local academic deployment and project demo setup.
EMS2 is developed in a common Windows web-stack environment with optional service integrations.
Windows 10 or 11, XAMPP, Apache, MySQL, PHP, and a browser such as Chrome, Edge, or Firefox.
VS Code or a similar IDE is used for coding, while Git supports version control and project tracking.
SMTP or PHPMailer, Razorpay-style payment support, Twilio, Python runtime, and Java runtime with Maven.
This environment keeps installation and testing accessible while still supporting multi-module architecture.
Detailed Description of the Technology Used
The core stack combines backend logic, persistent storage, and front-end structure for a web-based booking platform.
Handles routing, session management, controller flow, form processing, and dynamic page rendering for the main web application.
Stores users, venues, slots, bookings, reviews, and webhook-related records in a structured relational database.
Define page structure, styling, responsiveness, and client-side interaction across the public site and dashboard views.
Together, these technologies form the working foundation of the EMS2 website and dashboard experience.
The architecture also includes local server tooling, communication services, and auxiliary modules for future growth.
Provide the local execution environment for PHP and MySQL, making academic setup and browser testing straightforward.
Support OTP delivery, booking-related payment flow, webhook handling, and owner notification capabilities.
Extend the project with review sentiment scoring and concurrency-aware booking validation for future-ready architecture.
These modules make the system more serious than a basic CRUD demo.
They also create a clean path for future enhancements without redesigning the core platform.

and guided sign-in flow
Role-specific metrics, booking review panels, and management actions.
The current codebase defines dedicated views for home, venues, venue detail, login, register, OTP verification, bookings, and dashboard operations.
The overall workflow moves from discovery to authentication, booking, storage, and owner or admin review.
If the user is not authenticated, the system redirects to login or registration, verifies OTP, and then resumes the booking workflow without losing the intended action.
EMS2 is organized around customer, owner, and administrator actions with different responsibilities.
This role-based design keeps user journeys focused while still preserving centralized platform control.
The PHP application follows a modular structure using core classes, controllers, repositories, and services.
This separation of responsibilities improves maintainability and keeps request flow, data access, and integration logic organized.
The booking workflow coordinates UI, controller logic, repositories, and the database in an ordered sequence.

Activity logic:
1. Browse venues
2. Choose slot
3. Authenticate
4. Validate availability
5. Create hold
6. Create booking
7. Review outcome
